From Wiktionary, the free dictionary
See also: Malas, malās, målas, and Małas

English

[edit]

Noun

[edit]

malas

  1. plural of mala

Anagrams

[edit]
  • Alams, Lamas, Salam, Salma, Slama, almas, amlas, laams, lamas, salam

Albanian

[edit]

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • malësor (Standard)
  • malsor (Gheg)

Etymology

[edit]

From mal (“mountain”) (see also malësi (“highland”)).

Noun

[edit]

málas m (plural málas, definite málasi, definite plural málasit)

  1. (male) highlander, mountain dweller, mountaineer, alpinist
  2. (ethnography) resident of the malësi (“highland”) or of malësor (“highlander”) descent

Related terms

[edit]
  • malësi, malësia
  • mal
  • malësor, malësore
  • majë

Further reading

[edit]
  • “malas”, in FMGJSH: Fjalor i madh i gjuhës shqipe (in Albanian), 2026

Central Bikol

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Clipping of Spanish mala suerte or feminine plural of malo. Doublet of demalas.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • Hyphenation: ma‧las
  • IPA(key): /ˈmalas/ [ˈma.l̪as]

Adjective

[edit]

málas

  1. unlucky
    Synonyms: demalas, kablas, buwisit, maldito

Derived terms

[edit]
  • malason
  • mamalas
  • pagkamalas

Galician

[edit]

Adjective

[edit]

malas

  1. feminine plural of malo

Indonesian

[edit]

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • males (informal)

Etymology

[edit]

From Malay malas, from Proto-Malayo-Polynesian *ma- (“affix forming adjectives and stative verbs”) + below

  • From Prakrit [Term?] (compare to Hindi अलस (alas, “lazy, lethargic”)), from Sanskrit अलस (alasa).
  • Otherwise, probably from Proto-Mon-Khmer *las (“lazy, idle”).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈmalas/
  • Hyphenation: ma‧las
  • Rhymes: -las, -as, -s

Adjective

[edit]

malas (comparative lebih malas, superlative paling malas)

  1. indolent, lazy
    Synonym: berat tulang

Derived terms

[edit]
  • bermalas-malas
  • bermalas-malasan
  • kemalasan
  • malas-malasan
  • memalaskan
  • pemalas
  • termalas

Further reading

[edit]
  • “malas”, in Kamus Besar Bahasa Indonesia [Great Dictionary of the Indonesian Language] (in Indonesian), Jakarta: Agency for Language Development and Cultivation – Ministry of Education, Culture, Research, and Technology of the Republic of Indonesia, 2016

Tagalog

[edit]

Etymology 1

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • (Standard Tagalog) IPA(key): /ˈmalas/ [ˈmaː.lɐs]
  • Rhymes: -alas
  • Syllabification: ma‧las

Noun

[edit]

malas (Baybayin spelling ᜋᜎᜐ᜔)

  1. observation; intent look
    Synonyms: masid, malasmas, tingin, tanaw, sulyap
Derived terms
[edit]
  • ipamalas
  • magmalas
  • magmalas-malas
  • makamalas
  • malas-malasin
  • malasin
  • mamalasan
  • pagmalas
  • pagmamalas

See also

[edit]
  • matyag

Etymology 2

[edit]

From a clipping of Spanish mala suerte (“bad luck”). Compare Ilocano malas, Kapampangan dimalas, Central Bikol demalas, Cebuano demalas, and Hiligaynon dimalas.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • (Standard Tagalog) IPA(key): /ˈmalas/ [ˈmaː.lɐs]
  • Rhymes: -alas
  • Syllabification: ma‧las

Noun

[edit]

malas (Baybayin spelling ᜋᜎᜐ᜔)

  1. bad luck; misfortune; inauspicious
    Synonym: samang-palad
Derived terms
[edit]
  • kamalasan
  • malasin
  • pagkamalas
Related terms
[edit]
  • suwerte

Adjective

[edit]

malas (Baybayin spelling ᜋᜎᜐ᜔)

  1. unlucky
  2. unfortunate
See also
[edit]
  • buwisit

Further reading

[edit]
  • “malas”, in Pambansang Diksiyonaryo | Diksiyonaryo.ph, 2018

Anagrams

[edit]
  • Lasam, lamas
